title: Karnataka Moves on Drought Relief and Water Supply - Urban Acres
full_text:
Karnataka has expanded district-level measures for drinking-water supply, drought relief and fodder support after the state government said it had received no response to its request for Rs 22,400.58 crore in assistance from the Centre.
Revenue Minister and Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said on Friday that crop losses had been reported across 57.93 lakh hectares, with the total estimated loss placed at Rs 62,481.88 crore. Speaking to reporters after a review meeting at Vikasa Soudha, he said letters seeking meetings with the Union agriculture minister, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi had not received a response.
Parameshwara said the state would provide eligible farmers Rs 5,000 each in two instalments, with both instalments expected to be credited to bank accounts by December 1. Deputy Commissioners have been instructed to ensure that farmers included on the Green List receive the assistance within the stated deadline.
The review also focused on drinking-water preparedness. The government has released Rs 1 crore for each Assembly constituency and plans to provide another Rs 1 crore wherever required, according to Parameshwara. Deputy Commissioners have also been asked to use nearly Rs 379 crore available under the State Disaster Response Fund for water-related works.
Officials have been directed to drill new borewells where necessary and repair, renovate and clean existing ones. The state has asked districts to maintain adequate drinking-water supplies until May next year amid the possibility of an El Niño effect, as well as prepare for higher temperatures and a possible heatwave.
The government has spent Rs 26 crore on fodder kits and earmarked another Rs 33 crore for fodder kits and fodder purchases. Parameshwara said confusion arising from some officials’ interpretation of the relief instructions had been resolved.
